parameters.name: Pressure waveform
parameters.explanation: The trace shows airway pressure over time. Read it alongside the ventilator mode, flow and patient effort. Peak pressure during flow and plateau pressure during a suitable no-flow hold represent different measurements.

parameters.name: Flow waveform
parameters.explanation: The trace shows the direction and rate of gas movement. Check the display convention. Expiratory flow still present at the next inspiration suggests incomplete exhalation.

parameters.name: Volume
parameters.explanation: The volume display represents gas delivered or exhaled, depending on the measurement selected. Compare measured exhaled tidal volume with the expected value and consider leaks or measurement problems.

parameters.name: Respiratory rate
parameters.explanation: Check whether the value is the set frequency or measured total frequency. Total frequency can include patient-triggered breaths when the mode permits them. Compare it with the patient and waveforms.

parameters.name: Alarm limits
parameters.explanation: Alarm limits define monitored thresholds for parameters such as pressure or respiratory frequency. Assess the patient and cause of a breach before changing limits under the local protocol.

safety_concepts.text: Respond to every alarm by going to the patient; do not rely on silencing. If ventilation is inadequate and the cause is not immediately correctable, use the unit's emergency ventilation method and call for help.
Do not change alarm limits or modes unless authorised by order, protocol and training; extreme limits make alarms useless.

monitoring_concepts.text: Record set and delivered values, airway pressures, SpO2, end-tidal CO2 and waveforms at the policy frequency, and trends.

escalation_concepts.text: Call for help early for rising pressures, falling volumes, desaturation or distress.
